h1: Hydraulic presses — shop, H-frame, C-frame and straightening presses
intro: A hydraulic press drives its ram with an oil cylinder — slowly, with the full force available anywhere in the stroke and a pressure you set — which is why the same kind of machine presses bearings, straightens shafts, bends plate and punches, forms and deep-draws sheet in a die. NovoTech sells four kinds in Canada, each on its own page: hydraulic shop presses — the H-frame workshop press of every repair shop, dealer and fabricator, from a 10-ton bench press to 551 US tons; H-frame hydraulic presses — straight-side and four-column production presses for dies, deep drawing and composite moulding, from 55 to 661 US tons and to 3,307 US tons to order; C-frame hydraulic presses — open on three sides for small dies, punching and assembly, from 22 to 276 US tons; and hydraulic straightening presses — portal and 3-axis presses whose cylinder travels to the bend over beams, plate and shafts, from 22 to 441 US tons. The premium line is built in Turkey with European hydraulics and Siemens controls, the value line in China for the repair shop and lighter production. Below, the four kinds compared, every model in one table, the buying guide and the questions we get asked; every press comes with a CSA-approved panel and support from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Which kind of hydraulic press do I need?
faq.a: By the work. For pressing bearings, bushings and pins, straightening shafts and bending flat bar one part at a time, a shop press. For dies — forming, blanking, coining, deep drawing — run cycle after cycle under PLC control, an H-frame or four-column press, or a C-frame press when the dies are small and quick access matters more than table size. For beams, plate and long parts straightened where they lie, a straightening press with a moving cylinder. Send us the part and the force and we size the press.

faq.q: What tonnage shop press do I need?
faq.a: Most truck, equipment and fabrication shops run a 66 – 110 US ton press (DPM 1040-60 to DPM 1570-100, or the value-line HPP-60 and HPP-100): enough for pressing bearings and bushings, straightening shafts to Ø3″ and bending flat bar. Go to 165 – 220 US tons for large bearings, track pins, heavy shafts and forming plate. Beams and plate that need a moving ram are on the straightening press page.

An H-frame (straight-side) press is the stiffest and takes the largest tables and tonnages — the choice for deep drawing and big dies. A four-column (column) press is open on all sides for die access and automation. A C-frame press is open on three sides, so small dies go in and out quickly and the press takes less floor space; its table size is limited because the C deflects, which is why the premium-line C-frame range stops at 276 US tons.

The premium-line shop and production presses are built in Turkey with European hydraulics and Siemens controls, for daily production work, straightening lines and custom sizes. The value-line presses are built in China for the repair shop, the maintenance department and lighter production — the same tonnages at a lower price, with built-on or separate power units.

faq.q: Can the press be built to my die?
faq.a: Yes — every series of the premium line is built to order in the table size, stroke, daylight and tonnage the die needs, from a 33 US ton C-frame to a 3,307 US ton H-frame, with quick die change, die loading arms, ejector, heated platens or a die cushion as required. Send us the die drawing and the cycle you need and we quote the press around it.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models whose main motor is 2.2 kW (3 HP) or less — a machine with a motor above 2.2 kW must run on three-phase power and cannot be converted to 240 V single-phase. Manual machines have no electrics.
